mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1300K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST > 1300K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined signal of a tight labor market and strong job growth leads to increased wage pressures, higher inflation expectations, and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average, signaling a pickup in supply chain activity, leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate increased economic activity.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between INDPRO and GDP growth
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns following the trigger are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2.0% indicates slowing aggregate demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors reassess growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 annual growth < 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate exceeds 3.0% YoY, the combined signal of tight monetary policy and high inflation leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: the level of payroll employment (PAYEMS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as strong labor markets support consumer spending.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between PAYEMS and consumer spending
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly positively correlated with PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the annual growth rate of real disposable personal income (RSAFS) exceeds 4.0%, indicating strong demand, and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5.0%, the combined signal leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.
